newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor seeks speedy decision on Coega port.
newsitem.headline: Gencor seeks speedy decision on Coega port.

text.p: Gencor Ltd said on Friday it was considering a number of other sites for its 2.5 billion rand zinc refinery and needed a decision from the government soon on whether the proposed Coega port will be built.
South Africa's Department of Trade and Industry said earlier this week the project had been given support in principle and officials would now prepare details to put to Cabinet.
Gencor has been waiting since March for government approval of the Coega port -- the company's preferred site for a planned 220,000-tonnes-a-year refinery, near Port Elizabeth.
Gencor's Chief Executive Officer: base metals, John Raubenheimer, told Reuters that the company wanted a decision soon on the Coega project.
"What we are saying is that we need a decision on Coega soon for us to be able to consider Coega as an alternative site with these other two or three, to make our minds up," Raubenheimer said.
The alternative sites were at Port Elizabeth, East London and at Walvis Bay in neighbouring Namibia.

"If we can't get the thing done locally, then we may consider Walvis Bay. We have been in discussions with the Namibian authorities and they are very keen to get the thing there obviously," Raubenheimer said.
The Gencor board has yet to give approval for the zinc project.
All output from the zinc refinery would be destined for export.

Feasibility studies into the Coega bulk harbour and industrial zone have recommended that construction start early in 1998, leading to completion of the port and phase one of the industrial zone by 2001.
The scheme requires both the backing of government, which will have to raise the cash to provide basic infrastructure, and the commitment of a handful of risk-taking companies.
